step1_analysis.description: An output buffer circuit designed to adapt to different load capacitances while minimizing switching noise. It consists of parallel inverter stages (pull-up and pull-down networks) that can be selectively enabled to adjust drive strength.

paper_reference.title: Low Switching Noise and Load-Adaptive Output Buffer Design Techniques

t_rise.description: Rise time of the output signal (10% to 90% of VDD)

paper_reported.value: Not explicitly given, but evaluated under 40pF, 80pF, 160pF loads

sky130_expected.calculation: t_rise ≈ C_load * ΔV / I_drive. For 40pF load, ΔV = 1.44V, and PMOS drive current (W=5u, L=0.5u) ≈ 2.5mA. t_rise ≈ 40pF * 1.44V / 2.5mA ≈ 23ns.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Depends heavily on the load capacitance (40pF used as reference from paper) and the number of parallel PMOS devices enabled.

t_fall.description: Fall time of the output signal (90% to 10% of VDD)

sky130_expected.calculation: t_fall ≈ C_load * ΔV / I_drive. NMOS drive current is roughly 2x PMOS for same W/L. I_drive ≈ 5mA. t_fall ≈ 40pF * 1.44V / 5mA ≈ 11.5ns.
sky130_expected.reasoning: NMOS devices typically have higher mobility, leading to faster fall times compared to rise times for equal sizing.

t_pd.description: Propagation delay from input crossing 50% to output crossing 50%

paper_reported.value: Discussed as a key optimization metric

sky130_expected.calculation: Delay is approximately half of the rise/fall time for a lumped capacitive load.
sky130_expected.reasoning: The primary goal of the paper is to shorten delay time while managing noise, making this a critical metric.

sky130_expected.calculation: P_dyn = C_load * VDD^2 * f. For 40pF, 1.8V, and 25MHz input: P ≈ 40e-12 * 1.8^2 * 25e6 ≈ 3.24mW.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Dominated by the dynamic power required to charge and discharge the large 40pF load capacitance.

step3_testbench.description: Transient analysis to measure rise time, fall time, propagation delay, and average power of the output buffer driving a 40pF load.
step3_testbench.spice:
* Load-Adaptive Output Buffer Testbench
.lib "${SKY130_PDK}" tt

.param W_xm1=5u L_xm1=0.5u
.param W_xm2=5u L_xm2=0.5u
.param W_xm3=5u L_xm3=0.5u
.param W_xm4=5u L_xm4=0.5u
.param W_xm5=5u L_xm5=0.5u
.param W_xm6=5u L_xm6=0.5u

* DUT
XM1 N0 N6 GND GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm1} w={W_xm1}
XM2 N0 N5 VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm2} w={W_xm2}
XM3 N0 N1 GND GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm3} w={W_xm3}
XM4 N0 N1 VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm4} w={W_xm4}
XM5 N2 N4 GND GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm5} w={W_xm5}
XM6 N2 N4 VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm6} w={W_xm6}

* Power Supply
VVDD VDD 0 1.8

* Input Stimulus (25MHz, 1.8V swing)
VIN IN 0 PULSE(0 1.8 5n 0.1n 0.1n 20n 40n)

* Tie all control/input nodes together to enable maximum drive strength
V1 N1 IN 0
V4 N4 IN 0
V5 N5 IN 0
V6 N6 IN 0

* Load Capacitors (40pF as reported in paper)
CLOAD N0 0 40p
CLOAD2 N2 0 40p

.control
tran 0.1n 100n

* Measure Rise and Fall Times at main output N0
meas tran t_rise trig v(N0) val=0.18 rise=1 targ v(N0) val=1.62 rise=1
meas tran t_fall trig v(N0) val=1.62 fall=1 targ v(N0) val=0.18 fall=1

* Measure Propagation Delay
meas tran t_pd_hl trig v(IN) val=0.9 rise=1 targ v(N0) val=0.9 fall=1
meas tran t_pd_lh trig v(IN) val=0.9 fall=1 targ v(N0) val=0.9 rise=1

* Measure Average Power
let pwr = -i(VVDD)*1.8
meas tran avg_pwr avg pwr from=0 to=100n

print t_rise t_fall t_pd_hl t_pd_lh avg_pwr
quit
.endc
.end
